findings.evidence: Grep hits: new generic lemmas are at `WindingNumberReverse.lean:52`, `:63`, `:70`, `:75`, `:87`, `:94`; analogous generic PV API such as `HasCauchyPVAt.concat` is already in `CauchyPrincipalValue.lean:269`, while set-level API such as `HasCauchyPV.add` is in `CauchyPrincipalValueOn.lean:509`.
findings.fix: Move the three `...At` lemmas to `CauchyPrincipalValue.lean` and the three set-level lemmas to `CauchyPrincipalValueOn.lean`; keep `windingNumber_symm` and `IsNullHomologous.symm` in the reverse file importing that API.
findings.issue: The generic PV declarations `HasCauchyPVAt.symm`, `CauchyPVExistsAt.symm`, `cauchyPVAt_symm`, `HasCauchyPV.symm`, `CauchyPVExists.symm`, and `cauchyPV_symm` do not mention winding numbers and depend only on the PV definitions, so placing them in `WindingNumberReverse` makes basic PV API require importing later winding/null-homology material.

summary: The winding/null-homology reversal lemmas are naturally placed, but the PR hides broadly useful principal-value symmetry API in the winding-number reverse module instead of the canonical PV files.
